newsitem.title: USA: SCHUFF STEEL SEES LOWER Q3 REVS AND PRE-TAX INCOME.
newsitem.headline: SCHUFF STEEL SEES LOWER Q3 REVS AND PRE-TAX INCOME.

text.p: Schuff Steel Co said on Thursday that its third quarter pre-tax income and revenues may be lower than in the comparable quarter.

The company said it has experienced, and is expected to continue to experience, variations in quarterly and annual results of operations due to, among other things, the timing and terms of major contract awards and the starting and completion dates of projects.
The company added that its backlog decreased to $53.2 million at June 30, 1997 from $65.6 million at March 31, 1997 and from $98.5 million at June 30, 1996.

Scott Schuff, president and chief executive officer, said in a press release, "Our backlog of more than $53 million of business, as of the end of the second quarter, together with continued demand for the construction of new casinos, sport facilities and commercial and industrial plants, has required us to quickly focus on expanding our personnel and sales forces to capitalize on these opportunities."

"The company has recently expanded its engineering and design capabilities and fabrication capacity, updated its fabrication and detailing equipment and technologies and added sales and marketing personnel to support its continuing expansion," continued Schuff.
In addition, the company said it intends to acquire steel fabrication and erection companies which can provide a strategic and competitive advantage and that would be accretive to earnings.

Schuff concluded, "As we pursue our long-term growth strategy, we intend to explore potential acquisitions that would offer us increased plant facilities and opportunities to gain in market share in order to further penetrate domestic and international markets."
Schuff is a steel fabrication and erection company that provides a fully integrated range of steel construction services.
